study.question: Does the small apparent conditional utility of aligned task-union membership survive balancing feedback-stratum readout weights while preserving real content means, empty strata, valid-event mass and model capacity?
study.hypothesis: The counts-only control recovers most of the full-versus-blind click AUC gap. Frequency-dependent auxiliary readout weighting and membership-dependent scorer populations are still entangled. If useful aligned event grouping remains beyond numerical count weighting, full means should outperform uniform replacements under both actual and balanced occupied-stratum weights. The content-by-weight interaction will identify whether that incremental utility depends on empirical within-block proportions. This is a representation-use question: loader masks are deterministic functions of historical action codes and do not introduce a new information source. In the counts-only representation, the two occupied feedback rows have identical values and scores; their count-weighted sum depends only on total mass in exact arithmetic. Therefore continuous count magnitudes cancel, while empty-row patterns can still affect training Dice. The counts actual/balanced pair is an algebraic null control for BF16 weighting/reduction and subsequent training sensitivity.

nearest_work.difference: Primary DIN text lines58,81-88 and317-335 documents target-conditioned local activation and batch-distribution-dependent Dice. Inherit those components; test auxiliary-union compressed-row means crossed with post-mean mass balancing. No original DIN reproduction or priority claim.

Pinned benchmark forward lines123-139 initializes separate task hubs with task-mask-weighted sequence pooling. Here preserve the incumbent DIN-derived architecture, combine auxiliary masks into the inherited union and intervene only on compressed content/weights. No hub aggregation or broadcast layers copied; the original INFNet paper text is unavailable in the authorized archive.

Pinned forward lines112-140 pools history before global/group token mixing. Keep existing modules rather than introduce token mixing; all-valid block means are a matched-width replacement for member-conditioned means.

inherited_components: Entire strongest visible model, including item/action embeddings, uniform compression, target-match/moment details, towers, residual adapters and context-product modules
All folded Dice scorer operations and target-match normalization supports
Inherited four-task joint BCE and custom occupied-cycle context surrogate VJP; not the ordinary gradient of the displayed scalar loss
Prior counts-only representation replacement, including native empty-stratum pattern and all valid aligned event inputs
study.proposed_difference: A 2x2 factorial crosses native membership-grouped content means versus uniform means in each originally occupied feedback row, with actual feedback counts versus balanced readout mass. For total valid count n and k occupied feedback strata in each ten-event block, balanced mass is n/k per occupied row and zero for empty rows. Compute every native mean using original counts BEFORE this replacement; never recompute a mean using balanced weights. Apply consistently in three-, five- and seven-row compression. Uniform/support rows and all Dice input rows are unchanged by the weight factor at a fixed state. The content factor can change Dice population and auxiliary readout together; this study does not isolate those two paths.
predictions: Aligned event-content utility predicts AUC(full_control)-AUC(counts_control)>0 and AUC(full_balanced)-AUC(counts_balanced)>0; both remain preliminary at the fixed seed.

If count weighting explains the incremental content advantage, the content effect will substantially attenuate or reverse after balancing; report the difference-in-differences without treating one run as statistical confirmation.

At an identical parameter/buffer state, balancing leaves click probabilities unchanged in train and eval, since click reads uniform stratum0 and scorer input means/Dice populations are unchanged. Auxiliary readout and context cotangents may change, so full training trajectories can differ.
All four cells should retain32192421 learned parameters and identical state structure. Added arithmetic is only per-block post-mean weight balancing; measured runtime need not improve.

Counts_control versus counts_balanced should be algebraically equivalent at fixed state in real arithmetic: identical occupied means imply identical weights a, and (n0*a*u+n1*a*u)=(n*a*u). Different BF16 multiplication/reduction orders can break bit equality and amplify through training. Treat this as an arithmetic null control; do not interpret a nonzero final AUC difference as count-information utility.
falsifiers: Full membership fails to outperform the matched uniform-content control in both weighting strata, or the sign is unstable: useful event grouping is not supported in this setting.

Balanced count-only matches or exceeds full_balanced while the native content contrast is positive: membership utility is conditional on empirical weighting and cannot be attributed to event assignment alone.

Any mismatch in valid events, empty strata, target-match support counts, total feedback mass, initial learned tensors, number of training examples or frozen optimization invalidates the affected contrast.
A fixed-state click prediction discrepancy after changing only weights invalidates the proposed path separation and requires correction before performance interpretation.
alternative_explanations: Fixed-seed optimization variation and repeated validation selection; small AUC gaps have no available user-cluster interval or independent-seed estimate.
Counts-only keeps empty-slot patterns; balanced weights still reveal which strata are occupied. Neither is wholly membership blind.
The content factor changes both primary scorer Dice moments and auxiliary feedback representations; it cannot distinguish normalization-mediated utility from semantic retrieval.
Balancing changes auxiliary readout scale/composition and the resulting inherited surrogate VJP, potentially explaining click changes without a new forward information source.
Membership masks are derived from action codes already supplied; observed utility would concern an inductive bias under one-pass training.
Auxiliary tasks trade off against click: the strongest full model has worse auxiliary AUCs than DIN. A click improvement cannot establish general four-task superiority.
Shared normalization and training can affect empty-history validation predictions even though no membership event exists in such a sample; those slice changes are not direct local mask effects.

The counts-only actual/balanced pair changes finite-precision multiplication/reduction despite real-arithmetic equivalence. If its final metric gap is comparable to the full-versus-counts gap, the small semantic contrast lacks a demonstrated numerical robustness margin.
